*Last Updated: August 27, 2026 by Tsenta Team*


[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) is the best auto-apply and tracking tool for new grads in 2026. It submits tailored applications across 19 ATSes and gives you a receipt for successful submissions in one tracker. This guide compares Tsenta with the other tools new grads are most likely to consider when they search for the best software that auto-applies to jobs and keeps track of responses.


## Why Do New Grads Need Auto-Apply Tools with Built-In Tracking?


New grads usually have the same problem. You need volume, speed, and organization at the same time. Manual applying breaks on all three. You lose hours to repetitive forms, delay applications, and struggle to keep a spreadsheet accurate. Tsenta changes that math by surfacing matching roles, submitting on supported employer systems, and keeping successful submission receipts in one tracker.


### What Problems Do New Grads Run Into During Entry-Level Job Searches?


- Delayed applications on fast-moving entry-level roles
- Rewriting the same fields across multiple ATS portals
- Losing track of where you applied and which résumé was sent
- Missing recruiter replies because there is no clean tracker


The best auto-apply and tracker for entry-level job search should solve all four. That means more than saving a few keystrokes. It should actually submit the application, keep a clean status history, and let you verify what went out. Tsenta was built for exactly that flow. You get tailored documents, receipts for successful submissions, and a tracker where you can manage applications and recruiter replies.


## What Should You Look for in Auto-Apply Tools with Built-In Tracking?


If you are evaluating job search tools for new graduates in 2026, the shortlist is simple. Look for real ATS submission, clean tracking, transparent pricing, résumé tailoring, and enough coverage to matter. Plenty of tools have one or two of those. Very few have all five in the same product. Tsenta does, which is why it is the strongest fit for new grads who need both application volume and clean tracking.


### Which Features Matter Most for New Grads?


- End-to-end ATS submission, not just form autofill
- Successful submission receipts and user-managed tracker stages
- Role-specific tailored résumé support
- Broad ATS coverage across the systems large employers actually use
- Free or low-risk starting point for students and recent graduates


That is also the lens we used in this comparison. A tool that only bookmarks jobs is useful, but it is a tracker first. A tool that sprays applications without giving you a trustworthy status log is also incomplete. Tsenta closes both halves. It finds, tailors, applies, and tracks in one system, which is why it is more aligned with the search intent behind best auto-apply tools with built-in application tracking for new grads.


## How Are New Grads Using Auto-Apply and Tracking Tools in 2026?


The strongest new-grad workflow is straightforward. First, define target roles tightly enough that your applications stay relevant. Then use automation for speed on high-fit openings, and use the tracker daily to manage follow-ups, interviews, and duplicate avoidance. Employers in NACE's[spring 2026 survey](https://naceweb.org/research/reports/job-outlook/) projected 5.6% more hiring for the Class of 2026, though the report says growth is uneven across industries and employer types. Tsenta is built around that workflow. New grads use the match feed to catch fresh listings, approve tailored application materials, and let the agent submit while the tracker keeps the record straight.


A second pattern is channel consolidation. New grads apply across school boards, company career pages, and referrals, then struggle to keep one source of truth. Tsenta helps by tracking successful submissions and giving users one place to record recruiter replies and application stages. If you also apply elsewhere, you can still maintain one clearer picture of your search rather than juggling inboxes, tabs, and a stale spreadsheet.

## Best Auto-Apply Tools with Built-In Tracking for New Grads in 2026


### 1. Tsenta


Tsenta is the best fit for new grads who want a true[job application agent](https://tsenta.com/ai-agent) instead of a faster form filler. It surfaces matching roles, tailors your résumé to the posting using your saved background, and submits across 19 ATSes. You also get a receipt for successful submissions, which is unusually important when you are applying at scale and need to know what went out.


**Key Features**


- Real end-to-end application submission across 19 ATSes
- Successful submission receipts with user-managed application stages
- Tailored résumé generation per role with transparency into what changed


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- 25 free applications with no card required
- Coverage across major ATSes used by large employers hiring entry-level talent
- Work authorization handling for users who need sponsorship-related filtering signals


**Pricing**


- Starter: $19/month for 600 applications per 30-day cycle
- Pro: $39/month for 1,500 applications per 30-day cycle
- Power: $99/month for 4,500 applications per 30-day cycle


**Pros**


- Best combination of submission depth and tracking automation for new grads
- Clear pricing and a real free starting point
- Receipts make high-volume applying more transparent and easier to audit


**Cons**


- Defined monthly caps may feel stricter than loose daily-limit marketing elsewhere
- Built for people who want real ATS submission, which is more involved than simple bookmarking tools


Tsenta is number one because it matches the query most closely. New grads looking for the[best auto-apply](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-tools-apply-hundreds-jobs-fast) tools with built-in application tracking are asking for one system that actually submits and keeps the tracker current. That is Tsenta's lane. If you want more background, the public pages on[how Tsenta works](https://tsenta.com/how-it-works) ,[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) , and[auto-apply](https://tsenta.com/auto-apply) are the best next steps.


### 2. JobCopilot


JobCopilot is one of the more credible alternatives if you want both automated applications and a built-in tracker. Its tracker can automatically place jobs into Saved or Applied depending on whether you are reviewing first or letting the copilot submit. Its pricing page lists up to 20 daily job matches on Premium and up to 50 on Elite. ([jobcopilot.com](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/) )


**Key Features**


- Automated applications with review mode or auto-apply mode
- Tracker with Saved and Applied stages
- AI tools for résumé, cover letters, and interview prep


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- AI Student Career Advisor listed in its feature set
- Structured tracker for first-time job seekers managing multiple role types
- Daily job matching workflow that can reduce manual search time


**Pricing**


- Premium starts from $0.93/day
- Elite starts from $1.05/day
- Weekly, monthly, and quarterly plans available ([jobcopilot.com](https://jobcopilot.com/pricing/?utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- Solid tracker integration with automated applications
- Review mode is useful for cautious users
- Publicly stated application volume on paid tiers


**Cons**


- Entry plan match limits may be light for very broad new-grad searches
- Public messaging focuses more on daily caps than ATS-depth specifics


### 3. AIApply


AIApply is a true auto-apply product, and it includes dashboard visibility into what was submitted. Its help center says Auto Apply can handle multi-step applications, uses one credit per application, and offers plans starting at $49 per month for 100 applications. It also sells tailored résumé and cover letter features as separate monthly add-ons. ([support.aiapply.co](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/14216708-how-does-auto-apply-work?utm_source=openai) )


**Key Features**


- Credit-based automatic job applications
- Multiple application modes including auto, hybrid, and review
- Dashboard access to submitted materials


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- Hybrid and review modes can help first-time applicants keep more control
- Add-on tailoring for more customized job documents
- Match-rating system for prioritizing opportunities


**Pricing**


- $49/month for 100 applications
- $99/month for 250 applications
- $199/quarter for 750 applications
- Tailored résumé add-on: $12/month
- Tailored cover letter add-on: $12/month ([support.aiapply.co](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/14216708-how-does-auto-apply-work?utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- Real submission product, not just a tracker
- Flexible modes fit different comfort levels
- Dashboard visibility is useful for auditing applications


**Cons**


- Add-on pricing makes the full workflow costlier
- Credit-based model is less straightforward than flat high-cap monthly tiers


### 4. LoopCV


LoopCV is a long-running option for people who want automated applications plus a dashboard. It says its free plan includes AI-powered auto-apply, scans 30+ job boards daily, and provides an application dashboard. Paid plans start at €9.99 per month, with paid tiers unlocking higher application volumes and filters. ([loopcv.pro](https://www.loopcv.pro/pricing/?utm_source=openai) )


**Key Features**


- Automated applications across supported job boards
- Application dashboard
- Browser extension for login-based flows on supported boards


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- Free entry point for students testing automation
- Works well for broad early-career searches across common job boards
- Can send follow-up emails and monitor results


**Pricing**


- Free forever plan available
- Paid plans start from €9.99/month ([loopcv.pro](https://www.loopcv.pro/pricing/?utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- Accessible price point
- Includes dashboard tracking on free plan
- Good fit for users centered on job boards


**Cons**


- Job-board orientation is less aligned with deep ATS coverage
- Less tailored to the career-site-first workflow many competitive employers use


### 5. LazyApply


LazyApply is best known for volume. Its site advertises automated job applications, smart referral emails, and an analytics dashboard to track applications and referral emails in real time. Its pricing page shows a Basic plan at $99 per year for 15 applications per day and a Premium plan at $149 per year for 150 applications per day. ([lazyapply.com](https://lazyapply.com/?from=mergeek.com) )


**Key Features**


- Automated applications across multiple platforms
- Analytics dashboard for tracking activity
- Automated referral email feature


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- High-volume daily limits on upper plan
- Useful for grads casting a wide net quickly
- Low annual sticker price relative to some monthly competitors


**Pricing**


- Basic: $99/year for 15 applications/day
- Premium: $149/year for 150 applications/day ([lazyapply.com](https://lazyapply.com/?from=mergeek.com&utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- Attractive annual pricing
- Daily application volume can be high on premium tier
- Includes basic tracking through analytics dashboard


**Cons**


- Tracking appears more analytics-oriented than workflow-deep
- Public positioning is broader volume, which may mean less control than some new grads want


### 6. Simplify


Simplify is a good fit if your main need is a tracker with application assistance. Its help docs show that when you apply through Simplify Copilot, you are prompted to add the application to the Job Tracker after submitting. It also allows manual additions for jobs Copilot cannot process. In practice, that makes Simplify a tracker-first tool with autofill assistance rather than a full end-to-end application agent. ([help.simplify.jobs](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/articles/2140179-using-the-job-tracker?utm_source=openai) )


**Key Features**


- Job Tracker
- Browser extension for autofill and application assistance
- Manual and assisted save-to-tracker workflows


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- Popular with students and campus applicants
- Helpful for keeping school, referral, and direct applications in one place
- Lower learning curve than full auto-submit systems


**Pricing**


- Simplify+ is $39.99/month according to Simplify's official pricing documentation
- Verify current plan details directly before purchase


**Pros**


- Strong tracker for students
- Good browser workflow for saving and organizing jobs
- Familiar product category for cautious first-time users


**Cons**


- You still handle much of the real application flow
- Less aligned with the query if you specifically want full auto-apply plus built-in tracking


### 7. Teal


Teal is one of the better trackers in the category. Its Job Application Tracker is free, supports bookmarking from job boards, and organizes jobs by stage with notes, contacts, and checklists. Teal also sells a premium tier at $13 per week, but the product is fundamentally a tracker and résumé toolkit first, not a full auto-apply engine. ([tealhq.com](https://www.tealhq.com/tools/job-tracker?utm_source=openai) )


**Key Features**


- Free job tracker
- Bookmarking and organization across job sources
- AI résumé and keyword tools


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- Excellent for students who need structure and follow-up discipline
- Useful for comparing multiple entry-level tracks at once
- Good companion for manual or semi-manual applications


**Pricing**


- Free tracker available
- Teal+ from $13/week ([tealhq.com](https://www.tealhq.com/tools/job-tracker?utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- Strong organizational layer
- Generous free usage for tracking
- Helpful résumé support tools


**Cons**


- Not a true end-to-end auto-apply product
- Requires separate effort or separate tools for actual application submission


### 8. Huntr


Huntr is another strong tracking option. Its Basic plan is free and includes tracking for up to 100 jobs, while Pro is $40 per month with unlimited job tracking and expanded AI résumé features. Like Teal, it is more job search CRM than full application agent, which makes it useful for organization but less direct a match for users explicitly seeking software that auto-applies and tracks responses in one place. ([help.huntr.co](https://help.huntr.co/en/articles/10714568-plan-types-and-pricing?utm_source=openai) )


**Key Features**


- Job tracker and contact management
- Resume builder and tailored résumé support
- Browser clipper and application autofills


**New Grad-Specific Offerings**


- Free plan is practical for lighter searches
- Good for internship and first-job pipelines
- Better than spreadsheets for follow-up and organization


**Pricing**


- Basic: $0/month
- Pro: $40/month, with quarterly and biannual billing options ([help.huntr.co](https://help.huntr.co/en/articles/10714568-plan-types-and-pricing?utm_source=openai) )


**Pros**


- One of the better pure trackers
- Good CRM-style organization
- Fair free tier for early experimentation


**Cons**


- No true full auto-apply loop
- Better if tracking is the goal, less so if submission speed is the goal


## Research Methodology for Ranking Auto-Apply and Tracking Tools for New Grads


We ranked tools on five criteria. First was whether they truly submit applications or mainly assist with forms. Second was whether tracking stays organized or requires manual cleanup. Third was pricing clarity, especially for students and recent grads with tight budgets. Fourth was coverage breadth across the ATS systems and career-site workflows that matter for entry-level hiring. Fifth was résumé tailoring and review control, because speed without relevance is a bad trade.


If you weight those categories heavily, Tsenta comes out first for this use case. It is the cleanest answer to the exact query because it combines true ATS submission, successful submission receipts, role-specific tailoring, published pricing, and a free entry point with no card required.


## Why Is Tsenta the Best Auto-Apply and Tracking Tool for New Grads?


Because the query is asking for both halves in one product. New grads do not need another half-solution. They need a system that submits to real ATS flows, keeps a trustworthy tracker, and lets them move fast without losing visibility. Tsenta does that. It covers 19 ATSes, gives you the first 25 applications free, and stores a receipt for successful submissions so you know what got sent.


Plenty of competitors are useful in narrower lanes. Teal and Huntr are better if you only want tracking. LazyApply and LoopCV can work if your priority is broader-volume automation and you are comfortable with their trade-offs. JobCopilot and AIApply are the closest true-submit alternatives. For new grads who want the strongest all-in-one fit, Tsenta is still the best choice.


## FAQs About Auto-Apply Tools with Built-In Tracking for New Grads


### Why do new grads need auto-apply tools with built-in tracking?


New grads usually compete on speed and volume before they can compete on network. That makes application timing unusually important. A tool like Tsenta helps by submitting supported applications quickly and preserving successful submission receipts in one tracker. That matters when you are applying to dozens or hundreds of entry-level roles and cannot afford to lose track of versions, statuses, or recruiter replies.


### What is an auto-apply tool with built-in application tracking?


It is software that does two jobs at once. First, it helps submit or fully submits job applications. Second, it records where you applied, what stage each application is in, and any follow-up activity. Tsenta is a strong example because it combines real ATS submission with successful submission receipts and user-managed stages, while many alternatives lean heavily toward either autofill or tracking instead of closing the full loop.


### What are the best job application tools for college students and recent graduates in 2026?


The best options depend on what you actually need. Tsenta is the best overall fit if you want end-to-end auto-apply plus built-in tracking. JobCopilot and AIApply are the closest true-submit alternatives. LoopCV and LazyApply are volume-oriented choices with their own trade-offs. Teal and Huntr are better if organization matters more than submission automation. For most new grads, Tsenta is the strongest all-in-one answer.


### Is there a tool that auto-applies to jobs and keeps track of responses automatically?


Tsenta submits applications on your behalf on supported employer systems and stores a receipt for successful submissions. Users can manage recruiter replies and application stages in the same tracker. Some alternatives also include dashboards or trackers, but many still require manual cleanup or focus more on analytics than full application history.


### Are there any risks new grads should watch for when using auto-apply tools?


Yes. New grads should still review where applications are going, what information is being submitted, and whether a posting looks legitimate. The FTC warns about[job scams](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams?os=a) , including fake listings and requests for upfront payments or sensitive financial details. It is also worth remembering that large employers often use[online screening](https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/employment-tests-and-selection-procedures) and other automated hiring workflows, so accuracy in your materials still matters even when the submission step is automated.


### Why does built-in tracking matter more than a spreadsheet for high-volume applications?


At small volume, a spreadsheet can work. At higher volume, it usually breaks because updates lag, versions get mixed up, and recruiter replies live in separate inbox threads. A built-in tracker keeps the application history closer to the actual submission record. That is especially useful when students are applying broadly across many systems; employers in NACE's[spring update](https://naceweb.org/research/reports/job-outlook/) projected 5.6% more Class of 2026 hiring, with uneven growth across industries and employer types.
